367887.title: Elphick–Wocjan conjecture on the spectral lower bound for clique number
367887.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $
\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and let $
s^+$ be the sum of the squares of its positive eigenvalues:

$$
s^+ = \sum_{\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i^2.
$$

Let $\omega$ denote the clique number of $G$. **Elphick–Wocjan conjecture.** The positive-eigenvalue spectral quantity satisfies

$$
\sqrt{s^+} \leq n\left(1-\frac{1}{\omega}\right).
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\frac{n}{n-\sqrt{s^+}}\leq\omega.
$$

This conjecture strengthens Wilf's spectral lower bound on the clique number by replacing the largest adjacency eigenvalue with the square root of the sum of the squares of all positive eigenvalues. It is also stated as the second problem in a survey of open problems in spectral graph theory.

367966.title: Hill's crossing-number conjecture for complete graphs
367966.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{cr}(K_n)$ denote its crossing number, the minimum number of crossings in a drawing of $K_n$ in the plane or sphere. Define

$$
X(n):=\frac{1}{4}\Big\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2}\Big\rfloor.
$$

**Hill's conjecture.** The crossing number satisfies

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=X(n)=\frac{3}{8}\binom{n}{4}+O(n^3).
$$

This is a foundational unsolved problem in geometric graph theory. The conjecture was first studied by Hill in the 1950s, and the displayed quantity is attained by the standard conjectured optimal drawings; the equality is not known for general $n$.

368385.title: Freiman–Lev conjecture on restricted double sumsets
368385.statement:
Let $A=\{a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}\}$ be a set of $k>7$ integers such that

$$
0=a_0<a_1<\cdots<a_{k-1}
$$

and let $d(A)=1$ denote that the greatest common divisor of all differences between elements of $A$ is $1$. Write $2^{\wedge}A$ for the restricted twofold sumset, consisting of sums of two distinct elements of $A$.

**Freiman–Lev conjecture.** One has

$$
\left|2^{\wedge}A\right|\geq
\begin{cases}
a_{k-1}+k-2, & a_{k-1}\leq 2k-5,\\
3k-7, & a_{k-1}\geq 2k-4.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture concerns the minimum possible size of a restricted double sumset in terms of the largest element of a normalized integer set. The source attributes it to Freiman and Lev; no resolution is supplied here.

368535.title: Bonamy–Kardos–Kelly–Postle conjecture on fractional arboricity of planar graphs
368535.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $a_f(G)$ denote its fractional arboricity: the minimum ratio $p/q$ for which vertices can be assigned at least $q$ colors from a total of at most $p$ colors, with every color class inducing an acyclic subgraph. **Bonamy–Kardos–Kelly–Postle conjecture.** Every planar graph satisfies

$$
a_f(G)\leq 2.
$$

The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is refuted by a planar signed simple graph whose fractional balanced chromatic number is larger than 2; the construction also yields planar graphs with fractional arboricity exceeding 2.

368543.title: Conjecture that nontrivial snarks of high perfect matching index are strong
368543.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial snark, and let its perfect matching index be the minimum number of perfect matchings covering all edges of $G$. An edge of a snark is **suppressible** if suppressing it preserves the relevant snark structure; the snark is **strong** when all its edges are suppressible.

**Strong-snark conjecture.** With the sole exception of the Petersen graph, every nontrivial snark with perfect matching index at least $5$ is strong; equivalently, all its edges are suppressible.

The conjecture is motivated by computations on thousands of nontrivial snarks, all of which were found to be strong. It does not extend to the paper's low-cyclic-connectivity examples, which have perfect matching index $5$ but contain non-removable edges, and its general status is open.

368544.title: Conjecture on cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graphs attaining cycle covering ratio 7/5
368544.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph. Its **cycle covering ratio** is the minimum length of a cycle cover divided by $|E(G)|$. A cubic graph is **cyclically $4$-edge-connected** if no edge cut of size less than $4$ separates two subgraphs each containing a cycle.

**Cyclic 4-edge-connectivity conjecture.** Up to isomorphism, the Petersen graph is the only cyclically $4$-edge-connected cubic graph with cycle covering ratio $7/5$.

The conjecture is motivated by known infinite families attaining the ratio $7/5$, all with cyclic connectivity $2$ or $3$. Its status is open.

368599.title: Linear induced saturation conjecture for disjoint unions of chains
368599.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the chain poset with $k$ elements, and let $\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C_{i_j}$ be the disjoint union of chains with $i_1\ge i_2\ge\dots\ge i_m$. For a poset $P$, write $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,P)$ for the minimum size of an induced $P$-saturated family in $2^{[n]}$. **Linear induced saturation conjecture.** For any $i_1\ge i_2\ge\dots\ge i_m$, there exists $C=C(i_1,i_2,\dots,i_m)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C_{i_j})\le C\cdot n.
$$

At the time of the paper, it was unknown whether any poset has superlinear induced saturation number. If true, this conjecture is best possible because $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,2C_2)=\Theta(n)$ is known.

368614.title: The Graph Complement Conjecture for minimum rank
368614.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $G^c$ for its complement, $\operatorname{mr}(G)$ for the minimum rank of a real symmetric matrix described by $G$, and $\ord G$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**Graph Complement Conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{mr}(G)+\operatorname{mr}(G^c)\leq \ord G+2.
$$

This is a classical Nordhaus–Gaddum-type conjecture in minimum rank theory; the bound is sharp for paths, but the source gives no resolution in general.

368616.title: The Graph Complement Conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter $\nu$
368616.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $G^c$ be its complement, and let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum nullity among positive semidefinite matrices in $\mathcal{S}(G)$ satisfying the Strong Arnold property. Let $\ord G$ denote the number of vertices of $G$.

**Graph Complement Conjecture for $\nu$.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\nu(G)+\nu(G^c)\geq \ord G-2.
$$

The inequality is stronger than the corresponding minimum-rank conjectures because $\nu(G)\leq \operatorname{M}_+(G)\leq \operatorname{M}(G)$. The source gives no general resolution here, although later results in the paper establish conditional bounds.

368618.title: The strong $\delta$-conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter
368618.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree, let $l(G)$ be its degeneracy,

$$
l(G)=\max\\{\delta(H):H\text{ is a subgraph of }G\\},
$$

let $\lceil\delta\rceil(G)$ be the maximum of $\delta(H)$ over minors $H$ of $G$, and let $\nu(G)$ be the positive semidefinite Colin de Verdière parameter.

**Strong $\delta$-conjecture for $\nu$.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\delta(G)\leq l(G)\leq \lceil\delta\rceil(G)\leq \nu(G).
$$

The first two inequalities follow directly from the definitions, while the conjectural content is the final inequality. The source later says that the corresponding original $\delta$-conjecture is used conditionally and does not supply a resolution of this full chain in the candidate span.

368643.title: The compactness and deformation-dimension conjecture for CFT moduli
368643.statement:
Fix $c_0\geq 0$ and $E_{min}>0$, and let ${\cal M}_{c\leq c_0}^{E_{min}}$ be the moduli space of irreducible conformal field theories with central charge $c\leq c_0$ and

$$
\min\{p+q>0\mid H^{p,q}\neq 0\}\geq E_{min}.
$$

For a given CFT, its minimal versal deformation is a deformation with the smallest possible base. **Compactness and deformation-dimension conjecture.** ${\cal M}_{c\leq c_0}^{E_{min}}$ is a compact real analytic stack of finite local dimension, and the dimension of the base of the minimal versal deformation of any given CFT is at most $\dim H^{1,1}$. This conjecture proposes compactness of bounded-energy CFT moduli and a uniform local deformation bound; the source gives no resolution or evidence of a proof.

368710.title: Corona characterization conjecture for well-hued graphs
368710.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected well-hued graph, with independence number $\alpha(G)$, chromatic number $k$, and colorability sequence recording the maximum orders of induced $i$-colorable subgraphs. $$
a_2=a_1+2
$$

is the corona of the complete graph.

368801.title: Matheson–Tarjan domination conjecture for plane triangulations
368801.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane triangulation of sufficiently large order $n$. A dominating set is a subset $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $V(G)=\bigcup_{x\in X}N_G[x]$, and $\gamma(G)$ denotes the minimum cardinality of a dominating set.

**Matheson–Tarjan conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(G)\le\frac{n}{4}.
$$

Matheson and Tarjan proved the general upper bound $\gamma(G)\le n/3$ and gave examples showing that the conjectured constant would be tight; the conjecture remains open.
